concepts.title: Anand the Young Inventor
concepts.section: My Brother's Great Invention, Let us read
concepts.definition: Anand, a boy who believes he is a scientist, fills the house with homemade gadgets, from a water-bag burglar alarm to a full-size time machine, and never doubts that the next invention will work.
concepts.key_idea: Curiosity plus overconfidence makes Anand both a nuisance and a delight; his tinkering never stops.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr103.txt, My Brother's Great Invention, Let us read
question_patterns: draw a character sketch of anand the young inventor
why does anand love tinkering with gadgets
how did anand's burglar alarm backfire on his father
what does anand do when he is in one of his inventing binges
why did papa lock up his toolbox
what is anand's new project at the end of the story

solution_steps.explain: List what the character does and says at the key moments.
Match each action to a quality such as courage, kindness or curiosity.
Point to the exact lines of the text that support each trait.

concepts.title: From Burglar Alarm to Time Machine: Plot Events
concepts.section: My Brother's Great Invention, Let us read II
concepts.definition: The plot climbs from a soaked father to a real thief: the alarm drenches Papa, a film sparks the time machine, Boppa the sweeper breaks in one night, and the trapped machine room swallows him, leaving only a green scarf.
concepts.key_idea: Each invention raises the stakes: a prank device becomes the strange centre of an actual burglary.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr103.txt, My Brother's Great Invention, Let us read II
question_patterns: how did the burglar alarm work and why did it fail

who was the thief and how did the family find out
what happened when boppa entered anand's room
why was the time machine dismantled at the end
what was found near the panel of switches

solution_steps.explain: Note each invention and each misfire in the order they happen.
Mark the night the stranger enters and the trap is sprung.
Report what the family believes and what Anand insists happened.

concepts.title: Anita's First-Person Narration
concepts.section: My Brother's Great Invention, Let us read
concepts.definition: Anita, fourteen, tells the story about her brother with affectionate mockery; her doubts and warnings let readers judge Anand's inventions, and her voice turns family chaos into gentle comedy.
concepts.key_idea: A first-person narrator shapes sympathy: we see Anand as both a menace and a genius through Anita's eyes.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr103.txt, My Brother's Great Invention, Let us read
question_patterns: who narrates the story my brother's great invention
how does anita describe her brother's inventions
why does anita warn anand not to involve her
what does anita mean by let me put you in the picture

why was anita angry with anand during the theft

solution_steps.explain: Name who tells the story and her relation to the inventor.
Note the phrases in which she judges or teases her brother.
Say how her view colours the humour of every disaster.

concepts.title: Word Meanings: Tinkering, Sceptical and Crestfallen
concepts.section: My Brother's Great Invention, Let us learn
concepts.definition: Context fixes each word: tinkering means experimenting or fiddling with gadgets, sceptical means doubtful, a crestfallen look is a sad and disappointed appearance, and rigging up is assembling something temporarily.
concepts.key_idea: Every gloss word matches one of Anand's moods, from smug pride to crestfallen defeat.
concepts.textbook_ref: gepr103.txt, My Brother's Great Invention, Let us learn
question_patterns: what does tinkering mean in the story
who was sceptical about the burglar alarm and why
what is a crestfallen look
what does rigged up mean here
find the meaning of brandishing and cudgel
use the word frantic in a sentence about anand's workshop

solution_steps.explain: Find the sentence in which the new word appears.
Use the words before and after to sense what meaning fits.
Swap in the guessed meaning; if the sentence still works, it is right.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How did Anand mislead the thief, and why did it help?

solution_template.explain: Asked for the father's room, Anand points the intruder to his own room next door.
The false direction buys time for the children and lands the thief inside the humming time machine.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why did Papa get drenched at his own front door?

solution_template.explain: Anand rigged the alarm to trip only when the door opened gently, exactly Papa's habit.
The water bag loosened and soaked Papa, who then demanded to know who was behind the nonsense.
